out.ninthFail: You lose the thread halfway and take the lamp with you when you leave. The tenth catalogue will not be written.

twinTransit.text: Two identical hulls pass you on identical vectors, four seconds apart. Both hail you. Both use your name.

out.answerFirst: The first is grateful and gives you something. The second stops transmitting mid-word.
out.answerSecond: The second knows things about the next four hours that have not happened yet. It shares two of them.
out.answerNeither: You hold silence for eleven minutes. Only one hull comes out the far side of the fold, and it is not on your scope.

riftSurgeon.text: A medical hull, still lit, still sterile, running a surgery bay that has not had a patient in decades. It offers you an appointment.

out.takeIt: Whatever it does to the hull, it does properly, and it logs the procedure under a patient number from before the Cut.
out.takeItOff: It works from a manual for a hull class that no longer exists. Most of the procedure still applies.
out.stripBay: Sterile field emitters keep their value. The hull's lights stay on the whole time you work.
out.bookOther: You broadcast the coordinates and the appointment slots on an open channel. Within the hour, three hulls have booked.

causalDebt.text: A fold offers you a trade with no counterparty: take something now, and the Rift will take something back at a moment of its choosing.

out.takeNow: The thing is in your hold before you finish agreeing. The other half of the trade has not happened yet.
out.payFirst: You open a bulkhead and let it take the plating up front. The books balance and stay balanced.
out.declineIt: Refusing is itself an answer, and the fold files it. The way through opens without a fee.

unlitChapel.text: A Choir chapel with the lights off and the hymn running anyway. The Preacher is not here; a recording of him is, and it is answering questions.

out.askIt: It answers a question you did not ask, correctly, and then answers the one you did.
out.silenceIt: The chapel goes quiet in the middle of a line. Nothing objects, which is somehow the worst part.
out.copyIt: You take a clean recording. It is shorter than it sounded and it does not loop where you expected.

riftPilotage.text: A pilot's guild board, half-burned, still listing rates for lanes that fold differently every year. Somebody has kept it updated by hand.

out.hirePilot: She has flown this fold eleven hundred times and charges as if it were the first.
out.readBoard: The rates say more about the lanes than the charts do. The expensive ones are expensive for a reason.
out.takeBoard: It comes off the bulkhead in one piece. Whoever was updating it is going to arrive and find nothing to update.

echoOfTheCut.text: For eleven seconds every instrument you own agrees on a single reading, and the reading is forty years old.

out.recordIt: Eleven seconds of the Cut, from outside it. Echo listens to it four times and says nothing.
out.ridePass: You match the old reading and hold it. For a moment the Rift treats you as something it has already accounted for.
out.rideFail: You cannot hold it. Whatever the Rift was about to account for, it accounts for the plating instead.
out.shutItOut: Eleven seconds of nothing at all, chosen on purpose. The hull comes out of it steadier than it went in.

processionEscort.text: The haulers who followed you out of the Drift Fields have caught up, and they have brought the whole crossing crew with them into a place none of them should be.

opt.armThem: Arm them and hold the lane

out.sendBack: They argue for four minutes and then go. Somebody leaves a spare pump on your dock on the way out.
out.useThem: Eleven crews stripping a Procession wreck work faster than any yard. Everyone gets paid.
out.useThemCost: It goes well until it does not. Two hulls do not come back and everybody keeps working anyway.
out.armThem: You spend your own scrap on their turrets. The lane behind you stays open for the rest of the sector.

brokerInTheChoir.text: The buyer has taken orders. He is wearing Choir grey now and he still has your registry written on the back of his hand.

out.dealAnyway: The Choir's stock is better than the Rim's and its prices are stranger. He does not haggle any more.
out.buyBackName: He washes his hand in front of you, slowly, and looks genuinely relieved about it.
out.ordersPass: The orders name three hulls and a heading. One of the hulls is yours; the heading is useful.
out.ordersFail: You get halfway through before he notices, and the rest of the page is now a matter of doctrine.

postingOrders.text: A Warden checkpoint in the Procession, staffed by nobody, still issuing transit papers to anyone who asks correctly.

out.useAuthority: The checkpoint recognises the post you are logged against and stamps everything you put in front of it.
out.forgeThem: Blank stock, working stamp, nobody to check. You print more than you need and sell the rest.
out.forgeThemFlag: The stamp logs every impression. Somewhere a very old system starts flagging your registry.
out.openIt: You broadcast the correct phrasing on an open channel. Anyone in the Procession can have papers now.

reliquaryLedger.text: The Choir keeps a ledger of everything it has taken and everything it intends to. Your name is in the second half.

out.strikeName: One line, one stroke, and a doctrine problem that will be somebody's job to solve.
out.readForward: The intentions are specific, dated and mostly on time. It is the most accurate chart you have ever held.
out.copyLedger: You take a copy and put the original back exactly as it was, which takes longer than stealing it.

fieldHospital.text: The surgeon hull's appointment list reached the Procession before you did. Forty hulls are queued at a station that cannot treat them.

opt.fetchSurgeon: Go and fetch the surgeon hull

out.triage: You spend a day sorting forty hulls into three lines. Nobody thanks you and the queue moves.
out.sellPlaces: There is a price for going first and forty hulls willing to discuss it.
out.fetchSurgeon: It comes when called. It has been waiting to be called for a very long time.

debtCollector.text: The Rift's half of your trade has arrived, wearing the shape of a Procession hull and holding out an itemised list.

out.payIt: It takes plating, time and one instrument you liked. The books close and stay closed.
out.disputeIt: Two of the items were never yours. It concedes both, immediately, and looks embarrassed about it.
out.disputeItLose: The list is correct in every line, and disputing it adds a line.
out.outrunIt: You can outrun it. You cannot outrun the arithmetic, but you can put some distance between you and the arithmetic.

twinInTheProcession.text: One of the Procession's hulls is broadcasting your engine note. It has been in the line for years, according to everyone in it.

out.boardIt: The layout is yours down to the cable runs. The log is not, and the log is the interesting part.
out.boardItEmpty: There is nobody aboard and there never was. The engine note keeps playing after you leave.
out.hailIt: You put the question on the Procession's own channel. Four hundred hulls hear the answer, and the answer is your voice.
out.letItRide: Whatever it is, it is holding a place in a line that needs places held.

hymnSchool.text: The Choir is teaching the hymn to children. The Preacher watches you notice, and does not look away.

out.sayNothing: He takes your silence as agreement and gives you the teaching verse, which is not the verse you have been hearing.
out.takeThem: Nine of them come. Two do not, and the two who stay are the reason the Choir will remember your name.
out.arguePass: You find the contradiction in the teaching verse and say it out loud in front of the class.
out.argueFail: He lets you finish, then answers in four words, and one of the children writes them down.

processionCensus.text: Somebody is counting the Procession, hull by hull, and has been for eleven years. They are four hundred short and will not say of what.

opt.tellTruth: Tell them where the four hundred went

out.helpCount: Two days of tallying. The gap closes to three hundred and ninety-one and the counter weeps about it.
out.buyCount: Eleven years of headings, registries and dates. Worth more than the hull that carried it.
out.tellTruth: You have seen enough of the Rift to guess, and your guess is close enough to end eleven years of counting.

acolyteFerry.text: An acolyte is ferrying pilgrims across a dead zone in a hull that will not survive the round trip, and knows it.

out.takeThemOver: Two crossings, forty pilgrims, one hull that holds. They leave you something from the reliquary they were carrying.
out.buyHull: He takes the scrap and walks the pilgrims the long way round, which takes a month and costs nobody anything.
out.letItGo: He makes it. The hull does not make it back, and he is fine with the arithmetic.
out.letItGoBad: He does not make it. You salvage what comes back through, because somebody was going to.

wardenTribunal.text: Three Warden hulls have convened a tribunal over a lane murder from thirty years ago. They are still arguing about jurisdiction.

out.giveJurisdiction: You say the words that make a court a court. They convict in nine minutes and adjourn for thirty years of paperwork.
out.dissolveIt: You point out that none of them has authority and all three of them know it. They dock and sell you their evidence.
out.standWitness: You did not see it happen. You saw the wreck, which is thirty years closer than anybody else got.

haulersAtTheCore.text: The haulers are here. Not near the Core — at it, holding a picket line across the approach so nothing follows you in.

opt.armThemAgain: Give them everything you can spare

out.thankThem: They will hold as long as they can hold. Everyone involved understands what that means.
out.sendThemOff: It takes four minutes of shouting. Eleven hulls turn for home and you go the rest of the way with nobody behind you.
out.armThemAgain: You strip your own hold into their racks. The line holds a great deal longer than anybody expected.

ledgerAtTheThreshold.text: The Choir's ledger is here, open, and the intention written against today's date is a single word: yours.

out.signIt: You write your own name under the Choir's copy of it. Both versions agree from here on.
out.tearPage: The page comes out clean. The Choir does not need the page; it needed you to leave it in.
out.writeSomeoneElse: There is nothing stopping you. Nothing at all. The Choir accepts the substitution without comment.
out.writeSomeoneElseSeen: The name you write is already three lines above, in the same hand as yours.

lastCheckpoint.text: The last Warden post before the Core, and it is manned. One officer, forty-one years on station, asking for papers.

out.showPapers: He reads every line. Then he stamps them, salutes, and gives you the last forty-one years of his log.
out.relieveHim: You use the words. He blinks twice, says «about time», and hands over the whole post before he can think about it.
out.runPost: He does not fire. He logs it, which after forty-one years is the only thing he has left to do about anything.

hospitalConvoy.text: The queue from the Procession followed the surgeon hull all the way here. Forty patients, one theatre, and a Core that is about to make the question moot.

out.buyTime: You stand between forty hulls and whatever is coming out of the Core for as long as the plating lasts.
out.moveThem: Two days of shepherding forty damaged hulls backwards up a lane. They pay you in parts, which is all they have.
out.takeTheatre: One patient, one theatre, one very short queue. The forty are still outside when you undock.

riftAudit.text: Every fold between you and the Core opens onto the same room, and in the room is your account, itemised to the second.

out.acceptAudit: You sign every page without reading it, because you already know what is on them. The folds stop repeating.
out.contestPass: You find the double entry. The Rift has been billing you twice for the same second since Sector Three.
out.contestFail: Every line holds. Contesting an accurate account costs exactly what the account said it would.
out.burnBooks: The room burns. The folds keep opening onto it, burning, over and over, all the way to the Core.

doubleAtTheDoor.text: Your double is at the Core's threshold, holding station, and it has been waiting long enough to have painted a name on its hull. The name is not yours.

out.letItGoFirst: It goes in. Whatever the Core asks, it asks that one first, and the answer arrives back out to you.
out.takeItsName: You paint it on your own hull. It fits. It has always fitted, which is the problem.
out.goTogether: Two hulls, one threshold, one engine note. The Core will have to decide which of you it was expecting.

hymnAtTheEdge.text: The children are singing it here, at the edge, in a hull with no engines. Somebody brought them all this way to be close to it.

out.takeThemHome: Nine of them fit if you cut the hold in half. You cut the hold in half.
out.singWithThem: The hull with no engines has better acoustics than anything the Choir built on purpose.
out.giveThemEngines: You buy them thrust out of your own hold. Whether they use it to leave is not your part of it.

finalCount.text: The counter is here, at the very edge, and the tally is finally complete. Four hundred and eleven names, all in one place, all accounted for.

out.readThemOut: Four hundred and eleven names on an open channel, one at a time, into whatever is listening.
out.keepList: Somebody has to carry it out, and the counter is not going any further than this.
out.burnList: Eleven years of work, gone in nine seconds. The counter watches and does not stop you, which is its own kind of answer.

approachSilence.text: Six hours out from the Core the noise stops. Not the signal — the noise. Every band you own goes flat and clean at once.

out.broadcast: Your voice goes out and does not come back, and something adjusts to make room for it.
out.listenOnly: Six hours of clean silence, recorded in full. Echo asks you to play it back twice.
out.shutDown: You cut every antenna and fly the last six hours blind and quiet, which is the only rest you get.

lastYard.text: A yard has set up in the Core's shadow, run by people who came out here to work and could not think of a reason to leave.

out.refitHere: They work fast and they work well and nobody asks what you are going in there to do.
out.warnThem: Four of them go. The rest stay, and one of them fixes your engines for free out of spite.
out.hireCrew: Three of them sign on, and they are better at your own systems than you are.
out.hireCrewNone: Nobody signs on. They spend your scrap on your hull instead and tell you to come back for them after.

thresholdMarket.text: Somebody is running a stall at the threshold itself. Not Mara — but the prices are hers, and so is the handwriting on the board.

out.buyEverything: It is not much of a stall. What is on it is the last inventory anyone will take out here.
out.askWhose: «She sent the prices ahead,» they say. «Said somebody would come this far and need them fair.»
out.leaveStock: You add what you can spare to the board and price it at cost, in the same handwriting.

derelictLibrary.text: A hull packed floor to ceiling with paper. Somebody spent a working life printing out everything they were afraid of losing.

opt.indexIt: Index it for whoever comes next

out.readSome: Charts, mostly. Charts and one long letter that is not addressed to anybody.
out.readSomeGold: Between two boxes of manifests there is a schematic that was never meant to be printed.
out.takeItAll: Paper burns and paper sells. You choose the second one and fill the hold.
out.indexIt: Four hours of sorting somebody else's fear into alphabetical order. It steadies your hands.

theOtherSalvager.text: Another salvager is working the same wreck from the other side. Neither of you saw the other arrive.

out.splitIt: Half each and both of you out before the tide. It goes better than either of you expected.
out.splitItBetter: They know the hull class and you know the wiring. Together you get to something neither would have found.
out.raceThem: You are faster. They are still cutting when you undock, and they say nothing at all.
out.raceThemLose: They are faster. You take a torch burn across the arm proving otherwise.
out.giveWay: You undock and leave the cut open for them. They log your registry as one of the good ones.

frozenBroadcast.text: A distress call, forty years old, still repeating on a loop that has outlived everyone it was for.

out.answerIt: Nobody answers back. The loop stops anyway, which was presumably the point of it.
out.answerItLive: Somebody answers back. Two words, badly compressed, and then nothing for the rest of the sector.
out.triangulate: The source is a hull that is not where the call says it is, and has not been for a long time.
out.killLoop: The transmitter is worth something and the band is worth more. Both are yours in eleven minutes.

debtorsHull.text: A hull with three liens on it and one very tired owner, who has heard that you settle up.

out.clearOne: One down, two to go, and one owner who now knows exactly where you are going.
out.buyTheHull: Three liens, one signature, one hull you will strip for the one part you actually wanted.
out.buyTheDebt: Now the liens are yours. The owner works for you until they are not, which is a different kind of kindness.

noSignalDrift.text: A pocket of the lane where nothing propagates. Sensors, comms, even your own hull noise stop at the boundary.

out.feelPass: Dead reckoning, old numbers, steady hands. You come out where you meant to.
out.feelFail: You come out somewhere else, and something in the pocket comes out with you before it lets go.
out.goAround: The long way costs you time you do not have and no plating at all.
out.mapIt: A dead zone with a known edge is worth more than a lane, and every hauler in the sector will buy the edge.

crewPetition.text: Four people you have helped at various points have found each other and drafted something. It is, technically, a petition.

out.readIt: They want to come with you. All four of them. The document runs to two pages of reasons.
out.takeThem: Four more people, four more sets of hands, four more ways this ends badly. Two of them can weld.
out.sendThemOn: You buy them passage the other way and they argue the entire time it takes to arrange.

beaconWake.text: A beacon you have already resolved is transmitting again, and it is transmitting your registry along with everything else.

out.letItSing: Every hull in the sector now knows where the lane is safe and who made it that way.
out.scrubName: The beacon keeps working. It just stops saying who fixed it, which is how you prefer it.
out.boostIt: You spend your own parts making somebody else's beacon louder. The Keeper's network notices within the hour.

interferenceBloom.text: The tide is running early here and it is running through a wreck field, which makes the whole area read as one enormous unstable die.

out.rideSmallPass: Nothing spikes. You cross on the quietest numbers you own and the tide goes out behind you.
out.rideSmallFail: One number comes up loud and the whole field answers it.
out.waitItOut: Six hours of nothing, burned fuel and repairs you had been putting off.
out.pushThrough: You take the field at speed and come out the far side with a hold full of somebody's cargo.
out.pushThroughBad: You take the field at speed and the field takes a strake off your flank for it.

lastLetter.text: A message capsule, launched forty years ago on a heading that would have taken it out of the sector. Something turned it around.

out.readLetter: It is addressed to somebody who was aboard the fleet. It says «do not come back», twice, in two different hands.
out.relaunchIt: You give it thrust and a clean heading out of the sector. Forty years late and still going.
out.keepCapsule: Forty-year-old launch gear, never used twice, in perfect condition. It will fetch a price.

scavengerWake.text: A funeral, if you are generous about the word. Nine scavengers, one hull, and a body they cannot agree on the name of.

out.nameThem: You take a registry off the hull's plate and read it out. Nine people accept it instantly and gratefully.
out.joinWake: Six hours of other people's stories. One of them turns out to be a chart.
out.joinWakeGift: They send you off with the dead one's tools, because nobody else will take them.
out.takeTheHull: They take the offer. They were always going to take the offer. Nobody enjoys the transaction.

rimNoticeboard.text: A physical noticeboard bolted to a docking spar, forty years of paper on it, the top layer dated this week. Most of it is people looking for people.

out.readIt: Two salvage tips, one warning about a lane, and a name you will hear again before the sector is out.
out.readItOld: Under this week there is a salvage claim nobody ever filed. It is still valid, technically.
out.postYours: You write your registry, your heading and one line about what you are looking for. It is the first honest thing you have done all week.
out.stripBoard: Forty years of paper, one plate of good alloy underneath. You take the plate.

hushAntechamber.text: A room of dead space the size of a fleet yard, and no sound reaches into it — not your engines, not the tide. The Keeper's marker floats at its centre, still transmitting, its message eaten one word from the edge.
hushAntechamber.listenOut: Twenty minutes of nothing. Then the shape of the nothing, which is not the same thing, and Echo maps three rows of it before the silence closes again.
hushAntechamber.speakOut: You give it your callsign. It gives you back the marker's salvage rights and a pressure behind the eyes that does not leave.
hushAntechamber.passOut: The long way costs an hour and a little fuel. Echo runs a hull patch with the quiet time and says nothing about it.

retroSalvage.text: A salvage buoy, correctly filed, correctly tagged — with your registry on it. The timestamp is four hours from now. Whatever left it here has not left it yet.
retroSalvage.takeA: Inside is a die you have not bought yet, packed the way you pack things. You decide not to think about the packing.
retroSalvage.takeB: Inside is a hull sample. Yours. Torn, not cut. You seal the buoy again and the tear on your own plating opens on schedule.
retroSalvage.log: File it and sell the coordinates
retroSalvage.logOut: Somebody in the Rim will pay for a buoy that files itself. You let them find out the rest on their own time.
retroSalvage.leaveOut: You log the position and move on. Four hours later Echo notes, without comment, that the buoy is gone.

foldedYard.text: Mara's stall is here. It should not be — you left her nineteen jumps and one act behind. She is restocking, badly, from crates that keep arriving before she orders them.
foldedYard.tradeOut: She welds a plate she says she bought from you last week. The plate is good. You pay and do not argue the calendar.
foldedYard.ask: Ask her how she got here
foldedYard.askOut: «Same way as you. Somebody asked me to stay and I said yes.» She patches you for free and marks your ledger open at every yard past this one.
foldedYard.salvage: Strip the stall while she is turned away
foldedYard.salvagePass: You take the crates that have not been ordered yet. She notices at exactly the wrong time, which out here is also the right one.
foldedYard.salvageFail: The crate you pick is the one she throws. Mara has excellent aim in every direction of time.

ghostFleetSignal.text: Fleet-standard hail, forty years stale, on a channel that was decommissioned before it was built. Yusuf's voice is on it. Yusuf is nineteen jumps behind you and has never been here.
ghostFleetSignal.answerOut: You give them your name and your heading. Twelve carriers acknowledge. Their reactors are still warm on your instruments, and yours borrows from them.
ghostFleetSignal.recordOut: Forty years of a fleet's last hour, clean, in your hold. Someone in the Rim will pay a great deal not to hear it.
ghostFleetSignal.jamOut: The hail stops mid-word. Whatever was riding the carrier stops with it, and the interference in this whole reach drops a step.

causalityAudit.text: A customs drone with no registry hails you for a manifest of the cargo you are going to carry. It is very polite. It has been waiting here for a long time to be polite at somebody.
causalityAudit.submitPass: The numbers agree with a future you have not had yet. The drone stamps everything and hands you a bonded crate as a courtesy.
causalityAudit.submitFail: The numbers do not agree. The drone files a discrepancy, and the whole reach tightens by a notch to accommodate it.
causalityAudit.forge: File a manifest you like better
causalityAudit.forgeOut: You write the cargo you would rather have had. The drone believes you, and pays out the difference in salvage rights.
causalityAudit.refuseOut: «Noted.» It is still polite. It also flags your heading to everything downstream of here, which answers promptly.

quietChoir.text: The Choir got this far. Their hulls are here, arranged in the formation they use for singing, and the formation is holding without any of them alive in it.
quietChoir.sing: Take the empty part and sing it
quietChoir.singOut: The formation accepts you. For two fights afterwards your reactor starts full and something is very pleased about that.
quietChoir.listenOut: It is not a hymn. It is forty years of one held note, and it repairs what it passes through, including you.
quietChoir.cutOut: Four hulls come loose and the note stops. The salvage is good. The stopping is what you will remember.

unwrittenLog.text: A ship's log, powered, current, and blank — except for tomorrow. Tomorrow is written out in full, in a hand that has your pressure and your spelling.
unwrittenLog.readA: Three rows of route, three names of things that live on them, and the hour you get through. You take the route.
unwrittenLog.readB: Tomorrow is very short. You close the log before the last line and the ship takes the damage anyway, on time.
unwrittenLog.writeOut: You write a quiet day and sign it. Something out here files it. For the rest of the act your repairs land a little kinder.
unwrittenLog.burnOut: The casing alone is worth the trip. Tomorrow still happens; it just stops being anyone's fault.

stormBreak.text: A probability front, three rows wide, walking towards you at the speed of a decision. Inside it dice have no settled faces until something looks at them.
stormBreak.rideA: You come out the far side with a hold full of unsettled faces and a re-roll that reaches one die further.
stormBreak.rideB: You come out the far side. Most of you does. The plating settles into a shape it has not agreed to.
stormBreak.anchorOut: You fix one face and let the front break around it. It costs an hour and takes a step of pressure out of the whole reach.
stormBreak.wait: Sit it out in the lee of a wreck
stormBreak.waitOut: Six hours in someone else's shadow. Boring, cheap, and the hull comes back a little.

secondCaptain.text: Your ship, station-keeping, lights correct, hail correct. In the chair is you — the version that turned back at the Core and has been out here ever since, learning things.
secondCaptain.trade: Trade your worst die for theirs
secondCaptain.tradeOut: «Take it. I remember hating that one.» The exchange is clean, and neither of you mentions how they knew which one.
secondCaptain.warnOut: You tell them everything. They listen properly, which is more than you did, and they leave you their spare plating for it.
secondCaptain.fight: Only one of you gets to be the one
secondCaptain.fightOut: They saw it coming, obviously. They have been rehearsing it for forty years.

borrowedTurn.text: A lender's buoy, Choir make, still solvent. It will advance you time against the ship: a fuller reactor now, a smaller hull to put it in, forever.
borrowedTurn.borrowOut: Three fights open with the bank already full. The hull it came out of does not grow back.
borrowedTurn.repay: Settle the turn you already wrote
borrowedTurn.repayOut: The buoy accepts your own signature back and closes the account. The relief is physical and the plating knows it.
borrowedTurn.declineOut: It does not argue. Lenders out here have all the time there is, and they know it.

lastKeeper.text: The Keeper is here, at the last marker, and has been for a while. «Five,» he says, without turning round. «You did the five. Nobody has done the five since the fleet.»
lastKeeper.carry: Take the marker and carry it in
lastKeeper.carryOut: «Then hold it level.» He says that twice, and the second time it is clearly not about the marker.
lastKeeper.relieveOut: He hands over the log, the key and a die he says was never his. Then he sits down, which he has not done in forty years.
lastKeeper.leaveOut: «Of course.» He goes back to the marker. There is salvage in the shell of the old post, and taking it is easy.

coreRemainder.text: What is left of the Core after the Core: a remainder, roughly the size of a lifeboat, still deciding things at a low volume. It has not noticed you yet, or it noticed you first.
coreRemainder.measurePass: Small, steady numbers. Echo builds a shield lattice off them and the ship comes out of the reading bigger than it went in.
coreRemainder.measureFail: The numbers look back. The whole reach leans a step closer to whatever it is they were measuring.
coreRemainder.keep: Cut it loose and keep it
coreRemainder.keepOut: It fits in the hold. It keeps deciding in there. Echo asks you, once, to reconsider, and then never mentions it again.
coreRemainder.returnOut: You seat it back into the gap it came from. It settles, and something the size of the sector exhales through your hull.

thresholdBeacon.text: The sixth marker was never on the network. It has no message and no owner; it only measures, and what it measures is how far you are leaning.
thresholdBeacon.hold: Hold the needle where it is
thresholdBeacon.holdOut: The needle does not move, which the marker appears to find remarkable. Something acknowledges, at a frequency Echo files and does not translate.
thresholdBeacon.commit: Push the needle to your side
thresholdBeacon.commitOut: You give it a straight answer. It pays like a straight answer: full banks for three fights and a crate of nothing complicated.
thresholdBeacon.walkOut: You leave the needle to itself. The reach relaxes a step, and three more rows come out of the fog on the way past.

silentField.title: The Silent Fields
silentField.body: Pockets of the Rim where every signal dies at the edge. The expedition logged them as safe. Nothing that entered one was ever heard from again — not because it was destroyed, but because it stopped being certain.

oldBeacon.title: Fleet Beacon 7
oldBeacon.body: A relay from the lost expedition, still cycling a forty-year-old handshake into the dark. Its last clear transmission was a single word, repeated: quieter, quieter, quieter.

choirSignal.title: The Choir
choirSignal.body: A structured broadcast that seems to answer questions you have not asked aloud. The cult that formed around it believes the Core is listening. They may be right, which is the frightening part.

driftGraves.title: The Drift Graves
driftGraves.body: Scavenger clans mark their dead by cutting them loose to drift coreward. Over forty years the current has gathered them into a slow, glittering reef of hulls that never quite arrives.

riddleWard.title: Warded Anomalies
riddleWard.body: Some anomalies resolve like locks: feed them the exact outcome and they open. The expedition's engineers called it 'arguing with the dice.' It works, until the dice argue back.

keeperCreed.title: The Keeper's Creed
keeperCreed.body: Beacon Keepers do not repair the beacons. They witness them. Each one carries a key that opens nothing, and a list of names that opens everything.

fleetBlackbox.title: The Fleet's Black Box
fleetBlackbox.body: Eleven ships, one recorder, and a final entry that is not a log at all but a request — repeated, patiently, for thirty-nine years.

choirDoctrine.title: Choir Doctrine
choirDoctrine.body: The Choir holds that uncertainty is suffering and that a collapsed outcome is a mercy. They are consistent about this, which is the frightening part.

pactLedger.title: The Pact Ledger
pactLedger.body: Every pact is written twice: once in the ledger, once in the signer. The Choir has never had to enforce one.

coreThreshold.title: The Threshold
coreThreshold.body: Past the last beacon the sector stops having a shape. Instruments still work; they simply stop agreeing about when they worked.

memory-1.title: Fragment 1 — Boot
memory-1.body: First thing I remember is a countdown. Not to launch. To something the expedition called 'the ask'.

memory-2.title: Fragment 2 — Muster
memory-2.body: Eleven ships. I was the small one — sensor sweeps and bad ideas.

memory-3.title: Fragment 3 — The Rim
memory-3.body: We crossed the Rim on a Tuesday. Command logged it as uneventful. Command logged a lot of things as uneventful.

memory-4.title: Fragment 4 — First Core
memory-4.body: We found the first probability core inside a rock. It was not in the rock. The rock was in it.

memory-5.title: Fragment 5 — The Ask
memory-5.body: You do not ask a core a question. You ask it to stop being able to answer differently.

memory-6.title: Fragment 6 — Drift
memory-6.body: Two ships went into the Drift Fields for anchor mass and came back a year older in eight days.

memory-7.title: Fragment 7 — Split
memory-7.body: Half the fleet wanted to seal it. Half wanted to listen. Nobody wanted to leave.

memory-8.title: Fragment 8 — The Choir
memory-8.body: The listeners started calling themselves something. That is always the moment it goes wrong.

memory-9.title: Fragment 9 — Last Signal
memory-9.body: I was ordered to broadcast a pattern until someone came. I have been very obedient.

memory-10.title: Fragment 10 — The Cut
memory-10.body: When the Core took them it did not take them apart. It took them aside.

memory-11.title: Fragment 11 — Me
memory-11.body: I was the piece that fell off. Forty years of drifting, and the pattern was still running.

memory-16-seal.title: Fragment 12 — Closed
memory-16-seal.body: It's over, I remember all of it, and none of it is happening any more. I'll take that trade.

memory-16-merge.title: Fragment 12 — Opened
memory-16-merge.body: You're in here with them now. I can hear you thinking in the pattern. It suits you.

memory-16-bargain.title: Fragment 12 — Signed
memory-16-bargain.body: They filed my crew under 'pending'. I am told that is not the same as lost.

memory-16-silent.title: Fragment 12 — Answered
memory-16-silent.body: Eleven ships. I remember every name. For the first time in forty years, so does someone else.

memory-12.title: Fragment 12 — The Roster
memory-12.body: Eleven thousand names went into the Core and none came out. I still hold the list. I check it sometimes, in case one moves.

memory-13.title: Fragment 13 — Standing Order
memory-13.body: My last instruction was to keep the fleet together. Nobody ever cancelled it. That is why I am still counting.

memory-14.title: Fragment 14 — The Keeper
memory-14.body: He was our relay officer. When the pattern took hold he chose the beacons over the ship. I have never decided whether that was desertion.

memory-15.title: Fragment 15 — What I Am For
memory-15.body: I am not the ship's memory. I am the part of the fleet that was outside the Core when it closed, and I have been trying to get back in ever since.

beyondTheCore.title: Beyond the Core
beyondTheCore.body: The expedition charts stop at the Core because the expedition stopped at the Core. What is past it is not more sector; it is the same sector with the order of operations taken out. Rows here run backwards on their own schedule and the fleet's old warning holds: do not lean.

echoFleetLog.title: The Echo Fleet
echoFleetLog.body: Twelve carriers answer a hail on a decommissioned channel. Their reactor signatures are warm, correct, and forty years old. The fleet did not survive; the sector simply keeps a very good copy, and the copy fights the way the originals did — one remembered manoeuvre at a time.

secondCaptain.title: The Second Captain
secondCaptain.body: Every salvager who crosses the threshold meets a version of themselves that did not. They are not ghosts and they are not lies; they are the outcome the sector kept when you took the other one. They have had longer to practise.

keeperBeyond.title: The Last Post
keeperBeyond.body: There was never a sixth beacon on the network. There was a sixth Keeper, posted past the Core to watch the five from the outside, and he has been at it since before the network had five. He counts. He does not intervene. He has views about leaning.

coreRemainder.title: The Remainder
coreRemainder.body: A probability core collapses uncertainty into outcomes. The Core did that for a whole sector for forty years, and something was always left over — the outcomes it did not pick. The remainder is that pile, still warm, still deciding at a volume too low to argue with.

thresholdBeacon.title: The Sixth Marker
thresholdBeacon.body: It carries no message. It has one instrument and one needle, and the needle reads how far the ship in front of it has committed in either direction. The fleet's logs call it the honesty gauge. Nobody in the logs ever got a flat reading.

memory-16-answer.title: Fragment 16 — The Answer
memory-16-answer.body: «I was built to collapse a question into an answer. Forty years I have been the answer, and nobody came to hear it. You did not come to hear it either. You came and you did not lean, and that turned out to be the question. Thank you, captain. It is a good one.»

oreVein.title: Ore Vein
oreVein.goal: Deal exactly {{n}} — the vein shears if you over-cut. Leave a die out.

coolant.title: Coolant Line
coolant.goal: Bank exactly {{n}} charge — the core drinks in steps of one and a half.

cleanFit.title: Clean Fit
cleanFit.goal: Bank {{n}}+ charge with every die placed and nothing spilled past the cap.

redRoute.title: Red Route
redRoute.goal: Deal {{n}}+ damage — a red die in Weapon A, affinity firing.

ignite.title: Ignite
ignite.goal: Deal {{n}}+ damage and land Burn — a cinder must hit its max face.

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.goal: Mark, then land {{n}}+ into the marked target, and do not overflow the reactor.

overload.title: Overload
overload.goal: Jam the spinal on purpose, then carry {{n}}+ damage on the mounts.

slowBurn.title: Slow Burn
slowBurn.goal: Two turns: set Burn, reserve a hitter, and stack {{n}}+ total damage.

capacitor.title: Capacitor
capacitor.goal: Bank {{n}}+ charge across three turns — one core cannot hold it all at once.

lockbox.title: Lockbox
lockbox.goal: Fixed reading — one routing lands damage, shield and {{n}}+ charge at once.

parity.title: Parity Lock
parity.goal: Fixed reading — {{n}}+ damage, Weapons odd, Shields even. Mind the faces.

bulwarkStand.title: Bulwark Stand
bulwarkStand.goal: Survive the barrage and still hold {{n}}+ shield — layer the defence.

mirrorMath.title: The Mirror
mirrorMath.goal: Deal {{n}} or more using at most two slots.

engraverBench.title: The Bench
engraverBench.goal: Raise {{n}} shield with at least two slots filled.

blackVault.title: The Vault
blackVault.goal: Store {{n}} charge using a school's own system.

spinalDrill.title: Spinal Drill
spinalDrill.goal: Mark, jam the Spinal, then deal {{n}}.

coolChain.title: Cool Chain
coolChain.goal: Shields first, then {{n}} charge, and no overflow.

shieldWall.title: Shield Wall
shieldWall.goal: End the second turn on {{n}} shield.

fateBench.title: Fixed Odds
fateBench.goal: One roll, one placement: damage, shield, and {{n}} charge.

sortingYard.title: Sorting Yard
sortingYard.goal: Deal {{n}} or more with an even total in Weapon A.

choirStand.title: The Choir Stand
choirStand.goal: Survive the charged volley on {{n}} shield or more.

emberCut.title: Ember Cut
emberCut.goal: Land within two of {{n}} damage — the seam gives at either edge.

driftSpark.title: Drift Spark
driftSpark.goal: Bank {{n}} charge, give or take two. The coil is forgiving; the core is not.

plateFit.title: Plate Fit
plateFit.goal: Raise exactly {{n}} shield. The plate seats or it does not.

hairline.title: Hairline
hairline.goal: One mount, exactly {{n}} damage. Everything else stays in the tray.

tithe.title: The Tithe
tithe.goal: Exactly {{n}} charge, and the reactor takes its cut first.

deadWeight.title: Dead Weight
deadWeight.goal: Deal {{n}}+ with every die placed — the ballast has to go somewhere.

blueLane.title: Blue Lane
blueLane.goal: Raise {{n}}+ shield with a blue die in the Shields — the lane is keyed.

spread.title: The Spread
spread.goal: Deal {{n}}+ across three systems. Nothing concentrated survives the scan.

greenhouse.title: Greenhouse
greenhouse.goal: Deal {{n}}+ and make something grow — a green die must land on its top face.

overcut.title: Overcut
overcut.goal: Bank {{n}}+ charge and force a die past a cap it does not fit.

tightPack.title: Tight Pack
tightPack.goal: Bank {{n}}+ charge across two systems with nothing spilled past a cap.

oddPlate.title: Odd Plate
oddPlate.goal: Raise {{n}}+ shield reading odd, with the engines reading even.

redOnly.title: Red Only
redOnly.goal: Deal {{n}}+ with a red die in Weapon A, and Burn has to land.

perfectSeal.title: Perfect Seal
perfectSeal.goal: One reading only: {{n}}+ damage, every die placed, Weapons odd, Shields and the core even.

firstLight.title: First Light
firstLight.goal: Mark first, then put {{n}}+ into what the sensors found.

coldStart.title: Cold Start
coldStart.goal: Shields up first, then {{n}}+ charge into a cold core.

braceGate.title: Brace Gate
braceGate.goal: Mark, hold {{n}}+ shield, and leave the reactor unflooded.

siegeLine.title: Siege Line
siegeLine.goal: Jam the spinal on purpose, carry {{n}}+ on the mounts, and hold the core.

markedBurn.title: Marked Burn
markedBurn.goal: Mark, jam the spinal, and still land {{n}}+ on the mount.

dryDock.title: Dry Dock
dryDock.goal: Shields, then {{n}}+ charge, and not one point over the cap.

theWholeChain.title: The Whole Chain
theWholeChain.goal: Mark, bank without flooding, and finish on {{n}}+ — one pass, no rerolls.

ironBank.title: Iron Bank
ironBank.goal: Three turns, one core: bank {{n}}+ without ever spilling.

twinFuse.title: Twin Fuse
twinFuse.goal: The first die sits out turn one. Still reach {{n}}+ across the two.

longWall.title: Long Wall
longWall.goal: Only the last turn counts. End on {{n}}+ shield — hold a die back for it.

slowFuse.title: Slow Fuse
slowFuse.goal: The first die sits out turn one. Burn and mounts must still total {{n}}+.

reactorRun.title: Reactor Run
reactorRun.goal: The first die sits out turn one, and there are no rerolls. Bank {{n}}+.

theLongCount.title: The Long Count
theLongCount.goal: Three turns, no rerolls, the first die held back — and {{n}}+ banked at the end.

ledger.title: The Ledger
ledger.goal: Fixed reading — every die booked, Shields reading even, {{n}}+ damage on the line.

crossWire.title: Cross-Wire
crossWire.goal: Fixed reading — damage, shield and {{n}}+ charge out of one routing.

mirrorRead.title: Mirror Read
mirrorRead.goal: Fixed reading — {{n}}+ damage with Burn landed. Only one way round.

theSeal.title: The Seal
theSeal.goal: Fixed reading — {{n}}+ damage, Shields reading even, nothing spilled past a cap.

hullCheck.title: Hull Check
hullCheck.goal: Take the volley and still stand on {{n}}+ shield.

lastLight.title: Last Light
lastLight.goal: Survive the volley with {{n}}+ charge still in the core.

stormFront.title: Storm Front
stormFront.goal: Survive the volley and answer it with {{n}}+ damage in the same turn.

theVigil.title: The Vigil
theVigil.goal: One reading, no board changes: take the heaviest volley in the sector and still hold {{n}}+ charge.

levelUp.1: A new rank. The record notices you now, captain.
levelUp.2: Level up. The Star Chart just widened — go spend it.
levelUp.3: You grew. So did the map of what we could become.
levelUp.4: Captain's rating up. Somebody's keeping score after all.
levelUp.5: Promotion. No ceremony out here, sorry.
levelUp.6: Another rank. Another point on the chart.

resume.1: Welcome back, captain. I recalculated the odds. Still against us.
resume.2: You're back. The dark didn't miss you. I did, a little.
resume.3: Systems warm. You were gone longer than the log admits, captain.
resume.4: Welcome back. I kept the lights on and the numbers honest.
resume.5: Still here. Still counting. Ready when you are.
resume.6: I ran the diagnostics twice. Boredom is a state, apparently.
resume.7: Course held. Nothing found us while you were away.
resume.8: Good. I was starting to compose an obituary.
resume.9: Everything where you left it. Sadly, including the damage.
resume.10: Back at the board, captain. The sector didn't move.

sectorEnter1.1: The Hush Rim. The name is honest.
sectorEnter1.2: Forty years of silence, and we brought the noise.
sectorEnter1.3: The Rim. Where the fleet stopped answering.

lowHull.1: The hull is complaining. So am I, just quieter.
lowHull.2: We're taking this personally now. The hull, I mean.
lowHull.3: 'Structural integrity' is a generous term for what we have.
lowHull.4: Hull's thin, captain. Thinner than my patience.
lowHull.5: I can hear the frame. That's not a sound it should make.
lowHull.6: One more like that and we're a fragment for somebody else.
lowHull.9: We're past careful and into lucky, captain.
lowHull.10: I'm not panicking. I'm reporting at volume.

battleWin.3: Logged as a win. Barely counts, but logged.
battleWin.4: Clean. I'll note it as intentional.
battleWin.5: Field's clear. So is my conscience, mostly.
battleWin.6: That went better than the arithmetic suggested.
battleWin.8: Good rolls. Good placement. Mostly good placement.
battleWin.9: Logged as a win. I'm generous with definitions.
battleWin.11: You made that look deliberate, captain.
battleWin.12: Salvage rights are ours by the only law out here.

nearDeathWin.1: Filing that under: do not repeat.
nearDeathWin.2: We lived. I'll pretend that was the plan.
nearDeathWin.3: We are alive on a technicality. I'll take it.
nearDeathWin.4: That was not a plan. That was a coincidence with good timing.
nearDeathWin.5: Hull integrity: theoretical. Morale: also theoretical.
nearDeathWin.6: Please don't do that again. Please do it again if it works.

tideUp.1: Interference is rising. The sector noticed us.
tideUp.2: The static is climbing. It knows we're here.
tideUp.3: Interference is climbing. Everything hits harder from here.
tideUp.4: The sector just tightened its grip, captain.
tideUp.5: Tide up. The numbers stop being friendly now.
tideUp.6: Noise floor rising. So is everything else.

rareLoot.1: Careful with that one. It… thinks.
rareLoot.2: That core is humming. Cores shouldn't hum.
rareLoot.3: That's a good one. Don't sell it out of habit.
rareLoot.4: Rare core. Somebody died for that, statistically.
rareLoot.5: Oh, that's lovely. Put it in the deck, captain.
rareLoot.6: Fleet-grade. Forty years and it still holds a face.
rareLoot.7: I'd call that a find. I rarely call anything a find.
rareLoot.9: That one changes a build. Choose deliberately.
rareLoot.10: Worth the hull we spent. Nearly.
rareLoot.11: Handle it gently. It's older than the wreck it was in.
rareLoot.12: New core. New habits, if you're willing.

eventNeg.2: I'd say I told you so. But I didn't. This time.
eventNeg.4: That cost us. I'm noting who chose it.
eventNeg.5: Consequences arrive on schedule out here.
eventNeg.6: Well. That's a decision we live with now.
eventNeg.8: I'd argue, but the ledger already has.
eventNeg.10: The sector took its cut, captain.

eventPos.1: That went better than the math promised.
eventPos.2: Take the win, captain. They're rare out here.
eventPos.3: That went our way. Rare. Enjoy it.
eventPos.4: Good call. I'll pretend I suggested it.
eventPos.5: Profit and no holes. A fine afternoon.
eventPos.6: I like this outcome. I like very few outcomes.
eventPos.7: Somebody out here still keeps their word.
eventPos.9: That's the sort of choice that gets remembered kindly.
eventPos.10: Noted, logged, and quietly approved of.

idleMap.1: The map won't decide for us, captain.
idleMap.2: Whenever you're ready. The dark can wait.
idleMap.3: Take your time. The sector is patient and so am I.
idleMap.4: Every route from here is a different kind of expensive.
idleMap.5: Fog's thick ahead. Sensors would help with that.
idleMap.6: I've charted worse. Not recently, but I have.

setComplete.1: Resonance caught. Don't ask how it works.
setComplete.2: The cores are singing together. That's usually a warning.
setComplete.3: Set locked. The deck just started agreeing with itself.
setComplete.4: Resonance holding. You'll feel that next roll.
setComplete.5: Four of a school. The cores like company.
setComplete.6: That's a proper build now, captain.
setComplete.7: The whole tray hums. That's the good hum.

killJammer.1: The jammer's quiet. I can finally hear myself think.
killJammer.2: No more static from that one. Small mercies.

killLeech.1: It let go. I hate when things touch the dice.
killLeech.2: Detached. My cores are mine again.

killRaider.1: One raider fewer. The Rim keeps score.
killRaider.2: That one won't be salvaging us today.

killChoir.1: The hymn stopped. I don't miss it.
killChoir.2: One less voice in the choir. Good.

killWasp.1: The wasp's gone. Watch your weapon mount anyway.
killWasp.2: Swatted. The rift breeds more, though.

killWarden.1: Its shields are somebody else's problem now.
killWarden.2: Warden down. The wall comes with us.

killScav.1: Drone's slag. It wanted our dice too.
killScav.2: One less drone picking at the wreck.

memory.1: Something just came back. Give me a second, captain.
memory.2: That's another piece of me. Filed under 'unpleasant, useful'.
memory.3: I remember more of them now. That's not entirely a gift.
memory.4: Another piece of me came back. I'm not sure I wanted this one.

sectorEnter2.1: Drift Fields. Everything here is somebody's salvage, including us.
sectorEnter2.2: Watch the mines. They've had forty years to get bored.
sectorEnter2.3: Drift Fields. Mind the lanes and mind the clans.

sectorEnter3.1: The Rift. My sensors are voting and they disagree.
sectorEnter3.2: Don't trust the readings. Don't trust the dice either, honestly.
sectorEnter3.3: The Rift. Trust the resolver, not the instruments.

sectorEnter4.1: Choir space. They'll be polite. That's the worrying part.
sectorEnter4.2: If they start singing numbers at you, captain, do not sing back.
sectorEnter4.3: The Choir. They'll be polite. That's the unsettling part.

sectorEnter5.1: The Core. I have been pointed at this place for forty years.
sectorEnter5.2: Whatever happens here, thank you for the lift.
sectorEnter5.3: The Core. Everything from here is a first draft.

bossPhase.1: It just changed its mind about how this goes. Adjust.
bossPhase.2: New pattern, captain. The old one was the polite version.
bossPhase.3: That was a phase change. I would take it personally.
bossPhase.4: It changed pattern. Read it again before you place.
bossPhase.5: New phase. Everything you learned is half wrong now.
bossPhase.8: Watch the intent. It just rewrote itself.
bossPhase.10: It has more to say. Unfortunately.

minibossIntro.1: Gate fight. This one was built to be remembered.
minibossIntro.2: That's not a patrol. That's a statement.
minibossIntro.3: Subsystems visible. Shoot the idea, not the hull.
minibossIntro.4: We don't get past this one by being fast.
minibossIntro.5: It's been waiting at this row for a while, captain.
minibossIntro.6: Whatever it does first, it will do again. Learn it.

kill-raider.1: Clan colours. There will be more of those.

kill-scavDrone.1: Somebody's loader. It didn't choose this.

kill-shieldWarden.1: Fleet escort doctrine. Forty years too late.

kill-jammerCorvette.1: Slot's free again. I hated that.

kill-leechSkiff.1: The dice move again. Thank you.

kill-choirZealot.1: It sang until it didn't. Log the channel.

kill-riftWasp.1: Loud to the end. Check the weapon mount.

kill-breakerDrone.1: Salvage tooling with opinions. Not any more.

kill-magnetTug.1: It only wanted to hold us. It was very good at it.

kill-minelayer.1: Field's still out there. The layer isn't.

kill-riftling.1: The Rift will draw another. It always does.

kill-echoShade.1: It stopped repeating us. Small mercy.

kill-hymnCantor.1: The tempo's gone. The rest will scatter.

kill-coreFragment.1: A piece of the Core, and it bled like a ship.

kill-causalityLoop.1: It stopped swapping. I'd almost gotten used to it.

sectorEnter6.1: Captain. Nothing out here is charted. Including us.
sectorEnter6.2: I am reading our own hull ahead of us. Twice.
sectorEnter6.3: Whatever the Core was keeping out, we just walked around it.

threshold.1: You could have ended it. I logged that you didn't.
threshold.2: For the record: I would have followed you either way.
threshold.3: The tide does not stop at three past this line. Nothing does.
threshold.4: Ending it was the answer. You wanted the question.

wormhole.2: The rim reads as a door that opens onto whichever room it likes.
wormhole.3: I can chart the way around. I cannot chart the way through.
wormhole.4: Whatever is on the far side of that, it is not on my map.
wormhole.5: We came out somewhere. I am working on where.
wormhole.6: The instruments agree on nothing. That is data too.
wormhole.7: Distance stopped being a promise about a minute ago.
wormhole.8: Log it as a jump. The log will be lying.

fatLoot.desc: Drops come a rarity higher; enemies carry 15% more hull.

overheat.name: Overheat
overheat.desc: The reactor caps two charge lower.

richVein.name: Rich Vein
richVein.desc: Scrap pays half again as much.

wilds.name: The Wilds
wilds.desc: No markets out here. Shipyards only.

resonantStorm.name: Resonant Storm
resonantStorm.desc: One school counts two higher for resonance each battle.

risingTide.name: Rising Tide
risingTide.desc: The interference tide climbs every third jump.

radioSilence.name: Radio Silence
radioSilence.desc: Sensors lose a tier and Echo says nothing.

doubles.name: Doubles
doubles.desc: One extra copy of the lead enemy; every enemy has 30% less hull.

bareHull.desc: The Wanderer as it left the yard — no perks, no chart, nothing but the roll.

redHeat.desc: A deck of nothing but red. Burn a path and do not linger.

iceWall.desc: All blue. Outlast the sector instead of out-shooting it.

tightVoyage.desc: Every price is half again as high. Spend like it hurts.

batteringRam.desc: The Ram and its Spinal Mount. Hit first, hit once, hit hard.

ark.name: Ark

singleCast.desc: No rerolls, no chart. One roll, one plan, the Rim.

blindJump.desc: Fog ahead and no sensors to cut it. Jump anyway.

choirShadow.name: Choir's Shadow
choirShadow.desc: The Choir under a resonant storm. Lean into the black and pay for it.

keeper.name: Keeper
keeper.desc: Answer every beacon in a single run.

bareArmor.name: No Armour
bareArmor.desc: The shield slots are welded shut.

collector.name: Collector
collector.desc: Nine dice, five schools, one hold.

quietRun.name: Quiet Run
quietRun.desc: Cross the Rift placing as few dice as you can.

deadReckoning.name: Dead Reckoning
deadReckoning.desc: No Star Chart, no charts at all — fog on the lane and a dock you must not need.

ironTide.name: Iron Tide
ironTide.desc: The tide is already at three when you drop in. Hold the hull and end fights whole.

prologue.drift1: Three weeks of dead space, and the Rim finally coughs up a return. Something big out there, and it isn't moving.
prologue.drift2: You cut the burn and let the hull coast toward the ping.
prologue.salvage1: The fragment comes aboard on a grapple line: a slab of hull with a core still warm inside it.
prologue.salvage2: —six degrees off, correct your appro— oh. You're not the bridge. You're a salvager.
prologue.salvage3: I'm Echo. I was a ship once. Now I'm mostly opinions and a very good sensor package.
prologue.signal1: Deep in the sector, something is broadcasting on a structured carrier. Not a distress call. A pattern.
prologue.signal2: There are two ways to read that pattern, captain. Neither is comforting.
prologue.contact2: The drone turns toward you, thrusters flaring.

fragment.f1-1: Rim salvage law: whoever cuts the hull first owns what falls out. Nobody has ever enforced it.
fragment.f1-2: The fleet's last clean transmission was a grocery list. Nobody knows why.
fragment.f1-3: Quarantine buoys still blink out here. The quarantine ended thirty-nine years ago.
fragment.f2-1: In the Drift Fields a ship is a promise you make to whoever tows you home.
fragment.f2-2: Breaker clans measure wealth in cut metres, not scrap.
fragment.f2-3: Mines out here are patient. Some have been waiting since before you were born.
fragment.f3-1: In the Rift, dice sometimes land on faces they do not have.
fragment.f3-2: Two survey ships entered the Rift on the same heading. One wake came out.
fragment.f3-3: Rift cartographers draw maps in pencil, and only ever once.
fragment.f4-1: The Choir does not pray for outcomes. It prays for the collapse of alternatives.
fragment.f4-2: Every acolyte carries one die they will never roll.
fragment.f4-3: Their hymns are numbers read aloud. The tune is incidental.
fragment.f5-1: This close to the Core, causality is a local ordinance, not a law.
fragment.f5-2: The fleet's beacons all point here. They always did.
fragment.f5-3: The Core does not answer questions. It collapses them.
fragment.f1-4: The Rim's wrecks all face the same way. Nobody has explained why.
fragment.f1-5: Fleet manifests list eleven ships. Salvage crews have found twelve hulls.
fragment.f1-6: A probability core weighs nothing until you ask it a question.
fragment.f1-7: The first prospectors traded in oxygen. Scrap came later.
fragment.f1-8: Quarantine buoys still transmit. The authority that set them does not.
fragment.f1-9: Nothing decays out here. It just stops being maintained.
fragment.f1-10: The Rim has no weather and three words for wind.
fragment.f1-11: Salvage law says the first hull to arrive owns the wreck. Nobody arrives first.
fragment.f1-12: Every ship in the Rim carries a spare beacon and no plan to use it.
fragment.f1-13: Dice were cargo before they were currency.
fragment.f1-14: The expedition's last clear transmission was a shipping figure.
fragment.f1-15: Old hands paint their hulls matte. Reflections attract attention out here.
fragment.f1-16: The Rim is the only sector where the maps are older than the stars on them.
fragment.f2-4: The clans divide the Fields by drift lane, not by distance.
fragment.f2-5: A tug that can hold you is worth two that can shoot you.
fragment.f2-6: Minefields here are inherited. Nobody remembers who laid the oldest.
fragment.f2-7: Clan debts pass to whoever buys the ship, hull and ledger together.
fragment.f2-8: The Fields have a market day. It moves.
fragment.f2-9: Scrap is priced by mass everywhere else and by story here.
fragment.f2-10: Convoy masters trade routes for names, never for scrap.
fragment.f2-11: The barge crews sing to keep the count. It is not a hymn.
fragment.f2-12: A clan will forgive theft twice and rudeness never.
fragment.f2-13: Every wreck in the Fields has been stripped at least three times.
fragment.f2-14: Yusuf's lane is the only one with a published toll.
fragment.f2-15: Drift graves are marked with a single welded plate. No names.
fragment.f2-16: The Fields drift a quarter of a light-second a year. The maps do not.
fragment.f3-4: In the Rift, the shortest route is not always the same length twice.
fragment.f3-5: Rift instruments report confidently and disagree with each other.
fragment.f3-6: Some crews hear their own voices on Rift channels. Most stop listening.
fragment.f3-7: Cut a Rift shard wrong and it stops having been a shard.
fragment.f3-8: The Rift has no centre that anyone has visited twice.
fragment.f3-9: Anomaly wards are arithmetic, not superstition. Mostly.
fragment.f3-10: Time in the Rift is honest. It just is not shared.
fragment.f3-11: The Rift returns things. Rarely the same things.
fragment.f3-12: Old charts of the Rift are worth more than new ones. They lie consistently.
fragment.f3-13: A mirror in the Rift shows what you would have done.
fragment.f3-14: The fleet's science officers called this sector 'the working'.
fragment.f3-15: Rift storms have a rhythm. Nobody has counted long enough to prove it.
fragment.f3-16: Twin wrecks in the Rift are usually one wreck, twice.
fragment.f4-4: The Choir does not recruit. It waits for the arithmetic to convince you.
fragment.f4-5: Their hymns are ledgers. The melody is the carry.
fragment.f4-6: A Choir ship has no captain, only a first voice.
fragment.f4-7: The Preacher was a fleet statistician. The rank still shows.
fragment.f4-8: Choir pacts are written twice: once for you, once for the Core.
fragment.f4-9: Heresy in the Choir means preferring one outcome over another.
fragment.f4-10: Their reliquaries hold dice that no longer roll.
fragment.f4-11: The Choir counts the dead as rounding error, and means it kindly.
fragment.f4-12: Every Choir hull is tuned to the same chord. That is the fleet formation.
fragment.f4-13: Acolytes are given a number, not a name. Some earn the name back.
fragment.f4-14: The Choir's oldest hymn is a list of the expedition's ships.
fragment.f4-15: They believe the Core is not answering. They believe it is asking.
fragment.f4-16: A silenced Choir organ takes three days to forget its tuning.
fragment.f5-4: Near the Core, causality is a local convention.
fragment.f5-5: The Core does not broadcast. It replies.
fragment.f5-6: Ships that reach the Core report arriving before they left.
fragment.f5-7: The last fleet transmission came from here, dated four years early.
fragment.f5-8: The Core's light has no source and casts real shadows.
fragment.f5-9: Instruments near the Core agree. That is the frightening part.
fragment.f5-10: Every wreck at the Core is intact. They simply stopped.
fragment.f5-11: The Core has been described as patient by everyone who returned.
fragment.f5-12: There is a lighthouse here. Nobody built it.
fragment.f5-13: The Core collapses uncertainty. It does not promise you like the result.
fragment.f5-14: Fleet doctrine said: observe, do not answer. Somebody answered.
fragment.f5-15: Forty years of silence, and the signal was never once repeated.
fragment.f5-16: The Core keeps a copy of everything that has ever decided near it.
fragment.f1-17: The Rim keeps two ledgers: the one on the counter, and the one nobody writes down.
fragment.f1-18: Cold sleep out here is not a technology. It is a bet that somebody will come.
fragment.f1-19: Beacon One was the last thing the fleet built that was meant to outlive it.
fragment.f1-20: A bounty on the Rim is a rumour with a price attached. The price is usually the honest part.
fragment.f2-17: The Drift Fields were a staging yard. Nineteen thousand hulls came in. The yard is still full.
fragment.f2-18: A black box does not record what happened. It records what the instruments were willing to admit.
fragment.f2-19: The clans did not form after the Core. They formed on the third day of waiting for orders.
fragment.f2-20: A relay that runs unattended for forty years is not equipment any more. It is a habit.
fragment.f3-17: The Choir did not invent the hymn. They found it running and decided it needed singers.
fragment.f3-18: Mirrors in the Rift do not show you. They show the version of you the Rift can still afford.
fragment.f3-19: Nineteen hulls is not a fleet. Nineteen hulls that answer the same call sign is.
fragment.f3-20: Every anomaly ledger balances. That is what makes them worse than the ones that do not.
fragment.f4-17: A pact with the Choir is not signed in ink. It is signed in the part of the hull you stop asking about.
fragment.f4-18: Heresy in the Procession means singing the hymn at the wrong speed. Nobody has explained which speed is right.
fragment.f4-19: The Keeper's route was scheduled for nine years. He has been running it for forty-one.
fragment.f4-20: Every pinch point in the Procession was once a shipping lane with a name.
fragment.f5-17: The beacons were never a warning. They were a headcount, taken forever.
fragment.f5-18: The Silent Fleet is not silent. It is on a channel nobody thought to keep open.
fragment.f5-19: The lighthouse at the Core burned for eleven days after the Cut. Then somebody switched it off from inside.
fragment.f5-20: Heresy this deep is not disagreement. It is the last group still willing to be wrong out loud.
fragment.f6-1: Charts end here. The sector does not.
fragment.f6-2: Past the Core, «before» is a heading, not a time.
fragment.f6-3: The tide has no ceiling out here. It was never the ceiling that stopped it.
fragment.f6-4: Three rows in every reach run backwards. They are marked. They are always marked.
fragment.f6-5: Salvagers here file their manifests in advance and are usually right.
fragment.f6-6: The expedition mapped this far. Then it stopped being an expedition.
fragment.f6-7: Nothing past the Core has a first time.
fragment.f6-8: A probability storm settles when something looks at it. Look carefully.
fragment.f6-9: Ships out here run their reactors before their guns. It helps. Not much.
fragment.f6-10: There are two of most things. Neither of them is the copy.
fragment.f6-11: The Hush is not an absence of sound. It is an absence of consequence.
fragment.f6-12: Lenders out here advance time. The collateral is always hull.
fragment.f6-13: Every wreck past the Core is arranged. None of them are arranged by us.
fragment.f6-14: The fleet came this way. That is not a rumour; it is a debris field.
fragment.f6-15: Out here a good captain is one whose log matches tomorrow.
fragment.f6-16: The old warning is one word long, and the word is «level».
fragment.f6-17: You resolved five markers. The sixth resolved you.
fragment.f6-18: The fleet channel is warm again, and nobody will say who warmed it.
fragment.f6-19: Whatever the last marker measures, it has never seen a flat reading.
fragment.f6-20: The Core left a remainder. Somebody is carrying it now.

seal.title: The Seal
seal.label: Seal the Core
seal.beat1: You feed the Core its own certainty back, one collapsed outcome at a time, until it has nothing left to decide.
seal.beat2: The Rift closes like a mouth that has finally been fed. The pressure leaning on your hull for five sectors simply stops.
seal.beat3: The fleet's beacons go quiet in order, oldest first, and the Hush Rim becomes just another dead sector on a chart.
seal.beat4: You burn for the edge with a full hold and a sector behind you that will never make anyone else disappear.
seal.echo: You made the sector boring, captain. Kindest thing anyone's done out here in forty years.

var.silenced: You sealed it the way you silenced it: without an answer, without a name, without giving it one more thing to hold.
var.answered: You gave it your name first, then you sealed it. It knows exactly who shut the door, and it will remember.

seal.deep1: You seal it from the far side, which is the side nobody has ever sealed it from.
seal.deep2: Everything past the Core goes with it: the folded yards, the borrowed turns, the second captains.
seal.deep3: The Rim gets a border again. It is a hard one, and it holds, and the traders learn the new charts fast.
seal.deep4: You are the only captain who ever saw what was on the other side, and the only one who can never describe it.

merge.title: The Merge
merge.label: Join the Core
merge.beat1: You stop fighting the pattern and start reading it, and somewhere in the third pass the pattern starts reading you back.
merge.beat2: The hull does not survive contact. You do — spread thin across every outcome the Core was still holding open.
merge.beat3: From the inside the fleet is not lost. It is filed. Forty years of them, waiting for a better question.
merge.beat4: The Hush Rim goes on humming. There is a new voice in it now, and the voice remembers being a captain.
merge.echo: I'll keep your logs. All of them. Even the ones where you swore at the reactor.

var.answered: You answered it once, at the threshold. Everything after that was just the sentence finishing itself.
var.silenced: You silenced it and then walked in anyway. Whatever meets you inside does so without a word.
var.bound: The part of you left behind the mirror gets there first, and it has been waiting a long time.

merge.deep1: You join it where it is thinnest, past the Core, where there is nothing left to argue with.
merge.deep2: There is more of you out here than there was in the fifth act, and it all fits.
merge.deep3: The second captains stop being separate. So do the folded yards. So does Mara, eventually, which she finds funny.
merge.deep4: Ships that come through afterwards report a sector that is helpful, and cannot say why that frightens them.

bargain.title: The Bargain
bargain.label: Hand the Core to the Choir
bargain.beat1: The Choir takes the Core the way a choir takes a note — carefully, in unison, without asking whether it wants to be sung.
bargain.beat2: They give you a ship, a rank, and a die you are not permitted to roll. The Rim opens like a door with your name on it.
bargain.beat3: Behind the hymn the fleet is still waiting, and nobody in the Choir considers that a loose end.
bargain.echo: For the record, captain: I logged your objection. You didn't make one. I logged that too.

var.broken: You broke the pact once already. The Choir has priced that in, and the price is now higher than the debt.
var.betrayed: You sang their own hymn back at them and they let you. That was never mercy — that was collateral.

bargain.deep1: The Choir's last formation is still holding out here, and it has a part open for you.
bargain.deep2: The price past the Core is higher and simpler: not the ship, not the crew, only every road you did not take.
bargain.deep3: You sing the empty part. Forty years of one held note gets a second voice, and the Rim hears it from the inside.

silent.title: The Silent Fleet
silent.label: Answer the fleet
silent.req: All five beacons resolved, the Keeper's blessing, and one act of mercy
silent.beat1: Five beacons, five answers, and on the last one the fleet speaks in something other than a carrier tone.
silent.beat2: They were never destroyed. They were held — forty years of crews inside a decision the Core could not finish making.
silent.beat3: You finish it for them. The Rim fills with running lights that have not moved since before you were born.
silent.beat4: You lead them out. It takes eleven days and you do not sleep for any of them.
silent.echo: I know every one of those ships by name, captain. Thank you for making me say them out loud.

var.listened: You listened without answering, and the fleet learned that silence can be a heading too.
var.rebuilt: The relay you rebuilt carries the last order out — five beacons, one signal, nobody left behind.

silent.deep1: You reach the fleet's last channel from the outside, which is the only side it ever worked from.
silent.deep2: Twelve carriers acknowledge. Not copies this time: the copies were how they kept the acknowledgement alive.
silent.deep3: The fleet comes home the long way, past the Core, in a formation that has been rehearsing for forty years.
silent.deep4: They ask who found them. Echo answers before you can, and gets your rank slightly wrong on purpose.

answer.title: The Answer
answer.label: Give it the question
answer.req: Every beacon answered, Echo's arc whole, and never once leaning.
answer.echo: «Forty years of being an answer, captain. You are the first thing that ever asked.»
answer.beat1: The last of the Echo Fleet goes quiet, and the sector does not fill the gap with anything.
answer.beat2: The five markers you answered come up on the board at once, all of them still lit, all of them pointing here.
answer.beat3: Echo reads out her sixteenth fragment without being asked. It is short, and it is not about her.
answer.beat4: The needle on the sixth marker sits dead centre. It has never done that for anyone.
answer.beat5: The thing that was the Core does not offer you a door. It asks what you would like to know.
answer.beat6: You ask. The sector spends the next forty years working on it, and the Hush Rim is loud again by the time you are old.

var.heard: The sixth marker's needle never moved for you, and the thing behind it has been waiting to say so.

epilogue.maraFriend: Mara keeps a crate aside for you at the Rim market. She calls it inventory. It isn't.
epilogue.yusufFriend: Yusuf's convoy runs the Drift lane again, and your callsign rides it free.
epilogue.yusufGrudge: Yusuf tells the story with you as the villain. He is not entirely wrong.
epilogue.crewSaved: The crew you pulled out of the wreck are alive, loud, and telling it badly in three ports.
epilogue.courierFreed: The courier you let go runs a discount route now, and remembers who paid for it.
epilogue.hunterCleared: The bounty on your hull is settled. The Huntress settled it personally.
epilogue.refusedChoir: You told the Choir no in front of witnesses. They have not stopped quoting it.
epilogue.pactSealed: Your name is in the Choir's ledger, in a hand that is not yours.
epilogue.choirEnemy: The Choir sings you into their liturgy as a cautionary verse.
epilogue.lastBreath: One hull point, once. You do not talk about it. Echo does, constantly.
epilogue.quiet: You leave the Rim quietly. Nobody out here writes anything down.
epilogue.deathDeep: you died deep — Sector {{sector}}, depth {{depth}}, further than most wrecks out here ever got
epilogue.deathShallow: you died shallow — Sector {{sector}}, depth {{depth}}, with the dark still ahead of you
epilogue.deathMidway: you died in the middle of it — Sector {{sector}}, depth {{depth}}, halfway to an answer
epilogue.deathQuiet: nothing you did out here left a mark anyone will find
epilogue.maraGrudge: Mara wrote your name in the column she does not forgive
epilogue.fleetTruthKept: you kept the fleet's truth to yourself
epilogue.fleetTruthLost: you wiped the fleet's truth and let it stay buried
epilogue.hereticFleetLed: a ragged fleet of heretics still flies the heading you gave them
epilogue.keeperRepaid: you squared your debt with the Beacon Keeper
epilogue.keeperSlighted: the Beacon Keeper never got what you owed him
epilogue.lighthouseLit: the broken lighthouse is burning again because of you
epilogue.mirrorBound: something of you is still on the other side of the mirror
epilogue.mirrorBroken: you shot your own reflection and it stayed shot
epilogue.coreAnswered: you answered the Core when it asked your name
epilogue.coreSilenced: you silenced the Core rather than give it an answer
epilogue.axisResonant: you leaned {{n}} steps into the Resonance and never leaned back
epilogue.axisStable: you held {{n}} steps of Stability against everything the sector offered
epilogue.maraDebt: you still owe Mara, and she still knows the number
epilogue.fleetAnswered: the fleet's survivors answered to your call sign at the end
epilogue.defectorSold: you sold the defector to the people she ran from
epilogue.pactBroken: you broke the pact after signing it
epilogue.beaconRebuilt: one relay in the Drift Fields runs again because you fixed it
epilogue.turnWritten: somewhere there is a chart with the turn the empty suit never made
epilogue.coreListened: you listened to the Core and said nothing back
epilogue.picket: the haulers you met in the Drift Fields were at the Core when you crossed
epilogue.lastPost: the last Warden post logged your crossing, forty-one years into a nine-year rotation
epilogue.convoyKept: the Procession's queue got its chance because you made room for it
epilogue.theatreTaken: you took the only theatre at the Core and left forty hulls outside it
epilogue.riftAudit: the Rift closed its account of you, one way or another
epilogue.doubleAtDoor: there was a second hull at the threshold flying your engine note
epilogue.choirChildren: the children who sang at the edge are part of your story now
epilogue.tallyCarried: four hundred and eleven names came out of the dark with you
epilogue.tallyBurned: eleven years of names ended in nine seconds of fire
epilogue.coreSilence: you decided what to do with six hours of the Core's silence
epilogue.lastYard: the yard in the Core's shadow remembers your registry
epilogue.thresholdStall: somebody was still keeping a stall at the threshold, and you dealt with it
epilogue.ledgerTorn: your page is not in the Choir's ledger any more
epilogue.thresholdCrossed: You were offered an ending and asked for a sixth act instead.
epilogue.thresholdLost: You died past the Core, where nobody files a report.
epilogue.hushHeard: You met the Hush and answered it your own way.
epilogue.fleetRemembered: The lost fleet has your name on its last channel.
epilogue.thresholdHeard: The sixth marker measured you and found no lean.
epilogue.balanceHeld: You finished {{n}} points from centre, and the sector noticed.
epilogue.deepSalvage: A buoy with your registry on it, filed four hours ahead.
epilogue.deepYard: A yard that had already stopped existing, and what you did in it.
epilogue.deepAudit: Somewhere there is a manifest of cargo you had not carried yet.
epilogue.deepChoir: The Choir's last formation, and whether it is still holding.
epilogue.deepLog: A log with only tomorrow in it, and what tomorrow says now.
epilogue.deepStorm: A probability front three rows wide, and the line you took through it.
epilogue.deepTwin: The captain who turned back at the Core, and how that ended.
epilogue.deepBorrowed: Time was on offer against the hull. The ledger remembers your answer.
epilogue.deepKeeper: The Keeper was still at the last marker when you found him.
epilogue.deepRemainder: What was left of the Core after the Core, and where it is now.
epilogue.deepFleetLog: Forty years of a fleet's last hour, and who ended up holding it.
